lead: Digital systems often have many signals and only one wire to carry them. A multiplexer, or MUX, is a digitally controlled selector: n select lines choose one of 2ⁿ data inputs and pass it to one output. A demultiplexer, or DEMUX, does the reverse: it sends one data input to one of 2ⁿ outputs. Because the select code acts as an address, a MUX can also hold a truth table and generate any Boolean function. MUXes route signals onto shared buses, convert parallel data to serial, and drive displays.
prereq: You need: 5.3 for truth tables and minterms, and 5.2 for the AND-OR view of a logic circuit.

blocks.text: A multiplexer, or MUX, is a data selector. It has 2ⁿ data inputs I0 to I2ⁿ−1, n select lines S(n−1) to S0, and one output Y. The binary number on the select lines is the address of the input that reaches Y. A 2:1 MUX has one select line S and two inputs.

blocks.where: Y is the output; I0 and I1 are the two data inputs; S is the select line; S' is NOT S.

blocks.text: When S = 0, Y = I0; when S = 1, Y = I1.
A 4:1 MUX has two select lines S1 and S0 and four data inputs. Only one product term is 1 for a given select code.

blocks.where: S1 and S0 are the select lines; I0 to I3 are data inputs; Y is the selected input.

blocks.text: Many MUXes also have an enable input. An active-low enable EN' = 0 lets data pass. On a simple MUX, EN' = 1 forces Y = 0. To share one bus between several MUX outputs, the disabled outputs must go to high impedance (tri-state), not 0, so only the enabled MUX drives the bus.

Build a 4:1 MUX as a tree of three 2:1 MUXes. The first two 2:1 MUXes use S0. The upper one selects between I0 and I1; the lower one selects between I2 and I3. The final 2:1 MUX uses S1. It selects between the two intermediate outputs.

items: Connect I0 and I1 to the upper 2:1 MUX and use S0 as its select. Call its output U.
Connect I2 and I3 to the lower 2:1 MUX and use S0 as its select. Call its output L.
Connect U to input 0 of the final 2:1 MUX and L to input 1. Use S1 as its select.

blocks.text: When S1 = 0 the upper pair is passed; when S1 = 1 the lower pair is passed. The order is I0, I1, I2, I3 for select codes 00, 01, 10, 11. For the 4:1 tree above, the delay is two MUX delays: the two first-stage MUXes work in parallel, so their delays do not add. An 8:1 MUX with three select lines uses seven 2:1 MUXes, and the 8:1 tree has three MUX delays, one per stage.

sections.h3: Implementing a Boolean function on a 4:1 MUX

blocks.text: A 4:1 MUX can generate any three-variable Boolean function. Use two variables as the select lines and the third variable as data. The select code holds the truth table row group; the data input holds what F does inside that group. For variables A, B, C, put A on S1 and B on S0. Then each select code fixes AB and leaves C free.

items: Write F for all eight minterms.
In each group compare the two F values for C = 0 and C = 1.
Set the data input by the rule: 0,0 → 0; 0,1 → C; 1,0 → C'; 1,1 → 1.
Connect the four data inputs in the order I0 to I3.

blocks.text: The rule works because the MUX output is one product term: for select code 01, Y = I1. If I1 = C, the MUX outputs C when AB = 01; if I1 = C', it outputs C'. No gate is needed for the two select variables. This is function generation by table lookup.

A demultiplexer, or DEMUX, is a data distributor. It has one data input D, n select lines, and 2ⁿ outputs. The select code decides which output receives D; all other outputs stay 0. A 1:4 DEMUX has two select lines S1 and S0.

Its equations are Y0 = D S1' S0', Y1 = D S1' S0, Y2 = D S1 S0', Y3 = D S1 S0. A 2-to-4 decoder is the address part of this DEMUX. The decoder turns S1 S0 into four lines with exactly one line high: one-hot means exactly one line is 1 and all the others are 0. Tie D to the enable of the decoder and the enabled line carries D.

Applications: a MUX converts parallel bits to serial by selecting one bit after another; a DEMUX converts serial back to parallel. MUXes route one of many signals onto a shared bus. A seven-segment display uses a decoder or DEMUX to turn a code into segment or digit lines. Microcontrollers use MUXes to share pins and ADC channels; see 5.7.

figure.caption: A 4:1 multiplexer built from three 2:1 multiplexers. S0 chooses inside each pair, S1 chooses between the upper and lower pair.

spec.aria: A two-stage tree drawn with three node levels: the final 2:1 multiplexer at the root, the two first-stage 2:1 multiplexers below it, and the input leaves I0 to I3. The first-stage multiplexers use S0 to pick from input pairs I0, I1 and I2, I3. The root multiplexer uses S1 to choose between them.

examples.question: Implement F(A,B,C) = Σm(1,2,6,7) on a 4:1 multiplexer. Use A and B as the select lines, with A on the more significant select line S1. Find the connection for each data input I0 to I3.
steps: The minterms are 1, 2, 6 and 7. In binary A B C: m1 = 001, m2 = 010, m6 = 110, m7 = 111.
Write F for m0 to m7: 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1.
Group by AB. AB = 00 covers m0 and m1. F is 0 for C = 0 and 1 for C = 1, so I0 = C.
AB = 01 covers m2 and m3. F is 1 for C = 0 and 0 for C = 1, so I1 = C'.
AB = 10 covers m4 and m5. F is 0 for both C values, so I2 = 0.
AB = 11 covers m6 and m7. F is 1 for both C values, so I3 = 1.
Connect A to S1, B to S0, I0 = C, I1 = C', I2 = 0 and I3 = 1.
examples.answer: F is generated with A → S1, B → S0, I0 = C, I1 = C', I2 = 0 and I3 = 1.
examples.check:
minterms = [1, 2, 6, 7]
F = [1 if m in minterms else 0 for m in range(8)]
for v in F:
    print(v)

traps: Putting A on S0 and B on S1. The select code reads S1 S0, so A must drive the more significant line.
Trying to put all three variables A, B and C on the select lines of a 4:1 MUX. A 4:1 MUX has only two select lines; the third variable must feed the data inputs as 0, 1, C or C'.

Forgetting the enable input. An active-low enable EN' = 0 lets the MUX pass data; on a simple MUX EN' = 1 forces the output to 0. Sharing one bus needs tri-state outputs, which go to high impedance when disabled.
Calling a demultiplexer a multiplexer. A MUX has many inputs and one output; a DEMUX has one input and many outputs.
Assuming the decoder and the demultiplexer are unrelated. The 2-to-4 decoder is the address-selection part of a 1:4 demultiplexer; tie data D to the decoder enable to get the DEMUX.

quiz.q: How many select lines does a 4:1 multiplexer have?
quiz.a: Two select lines, S1 and S0.

quiz.q: Why can a 4:1 MUX implement a three-variable Boolean function even though it has only two select lines?
quiz.a: Two variables act as the address on the select lines. The third variable is assigned to the data inputs as 0, 1, C or C', so the MUX output follows the truth table.

quiz.q: Implement F(A,B,C) = Σm(0,3,5,6) on a 4:1 MUX with A and B as select lines. Give I0 to I3.
quiz.a: F for m0 to m7 is 1,0,0,1,0,1,1,0. Grouping by AB: I0 = C', I1 = C, I2 = C, I3 = C'.

quiz.q: A 4:1 MUX has I0 = 0, I1 = 1, I2 = C, I3 = C'. Select lines are A = S1 and B = S0. Write F(A,B,C) as a sum of minterms.
quiz.a: AB = 01 gives m2 and m3. AB = 10 gives m5. AB = 11 gives m6. So F = Σm(2,3,5,6).

quiz.q: A 1:4 DEMUX has D = 1, S1 = 1 and S0 = 0. Which output is 1?
quiz.a: Select code 10 sends D to Y2. Y2 = 1 and the other outputs are 0.

quiz.q: What is the difference between the select code of a MUX and the select code of a DEMUX?
quiz.a: Both are binary codes. In a MUX the code chooses which input reaches the single output. In a DEMUX the code chooses which output receives the single input.

quiz.q: Give one use of a MUX in data communication.
quiz.a: Parallel-to-serial conversion: the MUX selects one parallel bit after another and sends them on one line.

quiz.q: A simple 4:1 MUX has an active-low enable EN'. If EN' = 1, what is the output regardless of the data and select inputs? Explain.
quiz.a: The output is forced to 0. The disabled simple MUX does not pass any data input, so the select code has no effect. A tri-state MUX would instead put its output in high impedance.

beyond: Not for the exam. A lookup table inside an FPGA is a small memory that can be built as a tree of multiplexers, so the same idea appears in programmable logic. High-speed serial links use a serializer MUX and a deserializer DEMUX to move many bits over one pair. Search for multiplexer tree, serializer deserializer, and FPGA LUT to go further.
